To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have demonstrated for the first time that Pickering HIPE with high internal phase can be developed using hybrid protein/polysac charide particles as particulate emulsifiers, which can be potentially used as an alternative for PHOs to improve the oxidative stability of oil.
the Pickering HIPE can be stabilized by protein/polycarbohydrate hybrid particles and the emulsions are potential alternative for PHO.
Pickering HIPE stabilized by gliadin/chitosa hybrid particles can be a potential replacement for partially hydrogenated oils in food products.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of antioxidant Pickering emulsions (PEs), which can be used as potential alternative for partially hydrogenated oils (PHOs).
the development of Pickering high internal-phase emulsions (Pickering HIPEs), which are a new kind of emulsions stabilized by solid particles.
the synthesis and application of hybrid particles for the development of antioxidant Pickering HIPE as a potential alternative to PHOs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hybrid particles can be effectively applied as an efficient particulate emulsifiers for Pickering HIPE development.

this study has demonstrated the potential of using hybrid particles to prepare Pickering HIPE, and the developed Pickering HIPE can effectively protect the bioactive compound against oxidation, which is an important step toward the commercialization of these emulsions in food and cosmetic industries.
this work opens an attractive route to convert liquid oils into viscoelastic soft solid emulsions without artificial trans fats.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we successfully developed antioxidant Pickering high oil content Pickering emulsions with viscoelastic and gel-like features using a facile method.

the hybrid particles were prepared by a facile anti solvent method, the particles were used to prepare Pickering HIPE with high internal phases and good stability, the HIPEs showed viscoelastic and thixotropic properties and could be used as a potential alternative to PHO.
Pickering HIPE is an ideal candidate for food and cosmetic applications.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Pickering HIPE is a promising delivery system for bioactive compounds, especially those with low solubility in water, and the hybrid particles are promising candidates for the preparation of Pickering HIPOs.

we developed a new Pickering emulsifier, gliadin-chitosan hybrid particles, and used them to stabilize Pickering HIPE, and the Pickering HIPE was used to encapsulate curcumin and to protect the curcumin from oxidation.

Pickering high internal emulsions can be prepared with hybrid particles as a novel type of Pickering emulsifier and that they have potential applications as a food additive to improve the quality and safety of foods.
